messages.subject: Energy expenditure
parts:
Hello. One of my colleagues has asked me to investigate energy expenditure, believing that perhaps using this variable they will find a difference between treatment one and treatment two. 


using GGR package with duration of activity and differences in type of activity levels. I did not find a difference between two treatments. 


I know the ggir package is not catered for calculating energy expenditure

As seen here:


https://groups.google.com/g/rpackageggir/c/axygiBQpc60/m/_fCUqM50BgAJ


I note Vincent has noted his comments on reasons why we should move away from energy expenditure.


Is there any evidence to substantiate these claims? This would help me substantiate my reasons as to why I’m presenting my data based on duration of activity

messages.author: 017566be30afa7f3
messages.subject: Re: [GGIR] Energy expenditure
parts:
Hi Martinique,

Most of the energy prediction models are linear models, because there is no evidence that it needs to be non-linear. If you apply the same linear model to all your data then that by definition does not add information.

As a metaphor: if you multiply everyone's age by 2 and add 10 years then the new age variable will be equally correlated with any other measure of their anthropology or health compared with the initial age variable. We should not fool ourselves to think that we are measuring something different.

Secondly, attempting to estimate energy expenditure comes with most of the challenges I listed for MET in https://www.accelting.com/updates/why-does-ggir-facilitate-cut-points/. That blog post is about estimating time spent in ranges of energy expenditure but the problems are largely the same for estimating energy expenditure as a continuous outcomes.

Best,

Vincent




Dr. Vincent van Hees | Independent consultant | https://accelting.com/
